conventions: The ASV writes 'whether ... or' six times in this chapter, and the pair always goes to whatever connective morpheme stands in the Hebrew, never to a bein: to the waw in bein tov u-vein ra (27.12, 27.14) and in me-adam u-vehemah (27.28), and to the lamed standing where the connective stands in bein tov la-ra (27.33), headed on 'or' in each. Every bein in the chapter is unrepresented, because the ASV writes no word for the interval relation and a preposition of interval is not what 'whether' says (rules 14, 26, 40). Where the Hebrew writes a connective of its own for each member - im shor im seh (27.26) - each im takes only the word written for it and there is no pair to place; where no connective morpheme stands at all - mi-zera ha-arets mi-peri ha-ets (27.30) - both words are a single added unit headed on 'or'. Five of the chapter's BSB disagreements are these bein tokens and follow from this reading.

we-hayah hu u-temurato yihyeh qodesh (27.10, 27.33) writes hayah twice for one ASV 'shall be'. The chapter aligns that 'shall be' to the closing yihyeh, which stands where the English predicate stands, and marks the opening we-hayah unrepresented under rule 22. Rule 22's guidance about which occurrence is the rendered one is written for counted nouns and construct-headed phrases and does not reach a doubled verb, so the choice is recorded here. BSB attaches the word to the opening verb in both verses; that is the documented disagreement, not an error to fix.

Where the ASV completes a Hebrew substantive with a generic English noun the Hebrew does not write, that noun joins the substantive's unit and the head stays on the word carrying the lexeme: chamishit -> 'the fifth part' headed on 'fifth' (27.13, 27.15, 27.19, 27.27, 27.31), cherem -> 'devoted thing' and 'one devoted' headed on 'devoted' (27.28 twice, 27.29), qodesh -> 'a holy thing' headed on 'holy' (27.23). Rule 31's tie-breaker comes out the same way each time, because the ASV never writes 'part', 'thing' or 'one' alone for any of these words.

Two construct chains of identical shape are counted differently, and the ASV's number of 'the's is what separates them. shenat ha-yovel -> 'the year of jubilee' (27.17, 27.18, 27.23, 27.24) writes one 'the', which rule 29 fronts onto the rectum's article, leaving the construct noun bare. sheqel ha-qodesh -> 'the shekel of the sanctuary' (27.3, 27.25), achuzzat ha-arets -> 'the possession of the land' (27.24) and maasar ha-arets -> 'the tithe of the land' (27.30) write two, so nothing is fronted: the article takes the 'the' standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one. Do not level these to each other; the difference is in the English, not in the Hebrew.
report: Checked all 51 candidate lemma groups and read the full verse dump end to end for the added units the table is blind to (eight: 27.9 twice, 27.12, 27.15, 27.16, 27.24, 27.27, 27.30). Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the ASV's own wording or by a difference in the Hebrew. No split found, so no patches.

The 'whether ... or' family is the chapter's one construction analysed four ways, and each way answers to what stands in the Hebrew: the waw of bein tov u-vein ra (27.12, 27.14) and of me-adam u-vehemah (27.28); the lamed standing where the connective stands in bein tov la-ra (27.33); two written im in im shor im seh (27.26); and no connective morpheme at all in mi-zera ha-arets mi-peri ha-ets (27.30), where the pair is correctly one added unit headed on 'or'. Every bein is unrepresented, and rule 14's 'read sense and not position' is what rules out giving one of them the opening 'whether'.

asher ... mimmennah is one fused 'whereof' unit in 27.9 and three units in 27.11 ('of' on min, 'which' on asher, suffix unrepresented). The ASV writes one English word in the first and two in the second, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met only in 27.9. Not a split, and the BSB flag on the 27.11 suffix follows from it.

shenat ha-yovel -> 'the year of jubilee' (27.17, 27.18, 27.23, 27.24) and sheqel ha-qodesh -> 'the shekel of the sanctuary' (27.3, 27.25) are chains of identical shape treated oppositely: fronted in the first, arthrous in the second. The ASV's count of 'the's is what separates them, and rule 29 is applied the same way in all six phrases, achuzzat ha-arets (27.24) and maasar ha-arets (27.30) included. Recorded as a convention so a later pass does not level them to each other.

kol + lo fuses to a single 'no' in 27.28 and 27.29 under rule 35; 27.26 writes no kol, so there lo alone takes the 'no' recast onto the subject and ish keeps 'man'. The doubled hayah (27.10, 27.33), the infinitive absolutes ('indeed' in 27.13 and 27.19, nothing written in 27.31, 'at all' in 27.10 and 27.33), the fifteen object markers (all unrepresented), the four temurato/miqnato relative recastings and the suffix families are likewise all licensed.

BSB: 19 disagreements, none a genuine error. They are the lamed of leemor (rule 27), five bein (rule 26 and the convention below), object markers (rule 16), five articles for which the ASV writes no 'the' (rule 29), the two hayah, two resumptive suffixes (rules 22, 43), the second lo of 27.28, and the unintensified gaol of 27.31 (rule 56). Each rests on the ASV writing no English for the morpheme. Nothing was changed to raise the 97.1 per cent.
27.27 already carries the verse pass's own correction of a crossed pair; verified it now reads ka -> 'thy' and erke -> 'estimation', matching the parallel pair earlier in the same verse.

Promotions: none. The three judgments that looked general are already decided by the contract as it stands. The correlative pair going to the connective rather than to a bein is rules 14, 26 and 40 together; the supplied 'it be' joining the predicate's copula in a subjectless verbless clause (27.5, 27.6, 27.7, 27.9, 27.11, 27.12, 27.14, 27.26, 27.27, 27.33) is rule 20's own 'that it was good' example; and the wholly supplied 'shall be valued' of 27.16 being added, while the price beth keeps only its 'at', is rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause read against rule 49's subtraction test. Writing any of them into the contract would leave a cross-reference where the existing sentences already bind, so they are recorded as conventions instead.
